intro: Picture a small inn tucked into a shady tropical garden, a few minutes' walk from a long, quiet beach with the Sam Roi Yot mountains as a backdrop, and an owner who greets you by name from day one — Long Beach Inn is a small boutique inn in the Phu Noi Beach area of Sam Roi Yot district, Prachuap Khiri Khan province, about 40 km south of Hua Hin · this isn't a big resort with hundreds of staff, but a stay run by a foreign owner (Bram) who looks after guests personally, with around 33 rooms, a shady garden, a pool with jacuzzi, and a made-to-order breakfast that many reviews praise · what people keep mentioning is the quiet, the warm and easygoing service, and the fact that it's pet-friendly · from about THB 1,600/night, rated 4.7 from 269 reviews, and holding #2 of 16 hotels in Sam Roi Yot on TripAdvisor.

body.html: Long Beach Inn overview — who it's for — if we boil it right down, Long Beach Inn is a stay for "people who want to escape the chaos and settle in by a quiet sea, in a small place the owner runs themselves" · it's not a large beach resort packed with a water park and kids' activities, and it's not a town hotel where you step out onto a street full of shops · it's a small boutique inn of around 33 rooms in the Phu Noi Beach area of Sam Roi Yot district, set near Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park, only about 150 m from the beach · what sets it apart is that a foreign owner (reviews often mention the name Bram) runs the place and looks after guests personally, which gives the service the warm feel of a guesthouse rather than an ordinary hotel · it's still open and performing well, ranked by TripAdvisor at #2 of 16 hotels in Sam Roi Yot, rated 4.7 from 269 reviews, and a former Travelers' Choice winner · the real reviews line up on who fits here: couples after a quiet break, older travellers who like a calm atmosphere, nature lovers coming specifically for Khao Sam Roi Yot and Phraya Nakhon Cave, and people who want to bring a pet along · on the flip side, if you're after nightlife, luxury-resort amenities, or plenty of kids' activities, this may not be the most fitting choice · call it a stay built around "actually resting, without competing with anyone" at an accessible price — something that gets harder to find by the day as more beaches get developed and crowded.

Location and getting there — Long Beach Inn sits in Moo 4, Sam Roi Yot sub-district, Sam Roi Yot district, Prachuap Khiri Khan province, in the Phu Noi Beach area ringed by the limestone peaks of Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park · the appeal of the location is its quiet and its still-intact nature — several foreign reviews go as far as saying "Sam Roi Yot is Thailand thirty years ago," because the beach is still long, quiet and almost empty · on distances: from the inn it's about 150 m, or under a 5 min walk, to Phu Noi Beach; about 40 km, or roughly a 45 min–1 hr drive, south down from Hua Hin; and about 30 minutes from Pranburi town · from Bangkok it's around a 3–3.5 hr drive via Phetkasem Road · the key point reviews agree on is that this area is easiest with your own car, because there aren't shops or public transport around the inn that are easy to flag down like in town · the upside is that the owner and team can arrange transfers or take you to nearby sights, so even without your own car you can still get around · anyone without a car should arrange transfers with the inn in advance, since heading out for food or to other spots beyond the area almost always needs a vehicle · but seen the other way, this remoteness is exactly the charm that keeps the beach quiet and the sky clear.

"Stayed three nights and barely spoke to anyone except the owner, who was lovely. Woke up, ordered eggs and pancakes in the garden, walked five minutes to the beach, and there were only a handful of us on the whole stretch — this is what actually resting feels like, no fighting over a poolside chair."

Room types and decor — Long Beach Inn has around 33 rooms, all non-smoking, spread across low buildings around the garden, which keeps things airy and private · rooms come in several tiers, from the Deluxe Room as a comfortable standard, the Executive Room with more space, up to the Suite with Jacuzzi for those wanting something extra, plus a Bridal Suite style room for couples · every room has a private balcony, air conditioning, fridge, minibar, safe and free Wi-Fi · the decor leans simple and easy on the eye, with the warm tones of a seaside resort, and a balcony where you can sip coffee looking at the garden or listening to the sounds of nature · many reviews agree the rooms are clean, quiet and relaxing, well suited to actually getting some rest · to be straight about it, since this is an inn that's been open a fair while, some critical notes in reviews mention a few pieces of furniture starting to show their age, and dust in the air-con vents of some rooms · so if a brand-new room matters to you, ask about or request the most recently renovated room when booking, and set expectations to match a small inn that sells atmosphere and service over luxurious materials · for those who want something special, the Suite with Jacuzzi is the option reviews speak about positively for how relaxing it is.

Facilities, pool and activities — small as it is, Long Beach Inn still has enough facilities for a proper break · the highlight is the outdoor pool with jacuzzi set in the middle of a shady tropical garden, with a quiet feel that's more about easing in and relaxing than a big lap pool for exercise · around the pool are garden seating areas that many reviews praise as well-kept and shady · there's also a small massage room/spa, bike rental, a bar/lounge, free private parking and free Wi-Fi · the main thing guests do here is head out to explore the nature around Khao Sam Roi Yot — Phraya Nakhon Cave with its royal pavilion (Kuha Karuhas) inside the cave, Laem Sala Beach, the Sam Roi Yot wetlands, and quiet beaches nearby — and the owner helps suggest routes and arrange rides to nearby spots · to be honest, there are no family-resort kids' activities here, no water park or playroom, and the pool is more for relaxing than for play · a point reviews mention often is that the pool water is fairly cold even during the day, which some like for being refreshing, but those wanting a warm soak may need to rely on the jacuzzi instead · overall the facilities at Long Beach Inn work as a calm, shady backdrop to your break rather than a selling point built on excitement.

Food and bar — one of the things Long Beach Inn gets the most praise for is its made-to-order (a la carte) breakfast · instead of a buffet sitting under heat lamps, here you order what you want and it's cooked fresh in the kitchen — eggs done several ways, pancakes, bacon, and a Western-style breakfast — which many reviews call tasty and more special than the usual buffet · it's served in the morning, around 7:00–11:00 AM, with the option to eat in the garden or by the pool · the inn's restaurant also serves Thai and Western food for other meals, with a small bar/lounge for an evening drink · the honest point that comes up in reviews is that because the inn is in a quiet area with no restaurants within easy walking distance, the food options are fairly limited for anyone staying several nights · so if you're staying a few days, having a car to head out to seafood spots in the district, around Pranburi, or to local markets now and then helps keep things from getting repetitive · at times the menu may have fewer choices than a restaurant in town, since it's a small kitchen cooking fresh for the number of guests · overall, the food at Long Beach Inn sells on the fresh-cooked breakfast and the atmosphere of eating in the garden, while other meals are a convenient extra you should plan to balance with some meals out if you're staying a while.

Service — this is, without question, the heart and number-one selling point of Long Beach Inn · because it's a small inn where the owner runs the place and looks after guests personally, many reviews talk about the service as especially warm — the owner (reviews often name him Bram) is described as friendly, attentive, helpful, and able to give detailed advice on getting around Khao Sam Roi Yot · plenty of people were impressed that the owner arranges rides to nearby sights, suggests routes to Phraya Nakhon Cave, and treats guests more like friends than customers · another detail reviews mention fondly is the resident dog (named Bella) who welcomes guests, giving it the easygoing feel of staying at a friend's place · being pet-friendly also makes anyone wanting to bring a dog or cat along feel reassured · to be fair, since it's a small inn relying on the owner and a small team, some things may not be as systematic as a chain hotel, and you might have to wait a bit when the owner isn't on site · but overall, the service is the main reason this place holds #2 in the area and brings guests back for repeat stays.

What real reviews say (praise and criticism) — pulling from TripAdvisor, Booking.com, Agoda and Trip.com, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: a quiet location near Phu Noi Beach and still-intact nature, an owner and team who are friendly and attentive and look after you like a friend, a made-to-order breakfast that's tasty and feels special, a shady garden and a pool with good atmosphere, a solid base for Khao Sam Roi Yot and Phraya Nakhon Cave, and a pet-friendly stay that isn't easy to find · on the watch-out side: what comes up is furniture in some rooms starting to show its age and dust in the air-con vents of some rooms, which reflects an inn that's been open a long time and could use more upkeep · next is pool water that's fairly cold even during the day, limited food options for longer stays because it's far from shops, and value that some reviews see as depending on the room you get · these criticisms are mostly things you can manage by choosing your room and setting the right expectations (you come for the quiet, the atmosphere and the owner's service, not luxurious materials) rather than big problems that keep people from returning — and the fact that this small inn still holds #2 from 269 reviews is proof in itself.

"Clean place, the owner arranged a ride to take us round Phraya Nakhon Cave properly, and the made-to-order breakfast was really good · the only gripe is the room we got had furniture starting to age and the air-con was a touch dusty. Next time I'll try asking for a recently renovated room, but the service was good enough that I want to come back."

Price and value — the starting rate for a standard room is around THB 1,600/night at normal prices (in some periods and on some platforms it starts at roughly THB 1,400–2,000 depending on season and room type) · the Executive Room and Suite with Jacuzzi move up to around THB 2,200 and above depending on size and timing · compared with seaside stays in the Pranburi–Sam Roi Yot area, Long Beach Inn feels good value among small, quiet stays built around owner-run service, especially once you factor in the fresh-cooked breakfast, shady garden, pool with jacuzzi, being pet-friendly, and a location near Phu Noi Beach and Khao Sam Roi Yot · if you're a couple or a traveller chasing quiet and warm service on a modest budget, the money you spend comes back as experience · but if you're after a resort with full facilities, a flawless brand-new room, or full-on kids' activities, you may need to weigh it against the area's larger beach resorts like Dolphin Bay or the higher-priced resorts on the Pranburi side · the value here comes down to how much you prize "the quiet and the owner's service."

What to know before booking — a few things help the stay go smoothly · one, having your own car is easiest, since the inn is in a quiet area far from shops and public transport; without a car, arrange transfers with the inn in advance · two, if a newer room matters to you, request the most recently renovated room at the time of booking, since some rooms have aging furniture and dust in the air-con vents · three, if you're staying several nights, plan your meals to include some eating out, since the inn's options are limited and there are no restaurants within walking distance · four, the pool is fairly cold — if you like warm water, use the jacuzzi instead · five, if you're bringing a pet, tell the inn at booking since it's pet-friendly · six, you can book trips to Khao Sam Roi Yot and Phraya Nakhon Cave through the inn for convenience, and you should book rooms ahead during long holidays since a small place fills up fast · seven, check in from midday to evening (around 12:00 PM onward) and check out before noon, and let them know your arrival time in advance since it's a small, owner-run inn.

Summary — from all the real reviews, Long Beach Inn is the best fit for couples and travellers who want a quiet seaside break in a small, owner-run stay, with a base for exploring Khao Sam Roi Yot · a location near Phu Noi Beach, a shady garden, a pool with jacuzzi, a made-to-order breakfast, warm owner-led service, and being pet-friendly give it a charm of its own that's kept it at #2 in the area · if you're after a big resort with full kids' activities, freshly designed rooms, or nightlife and a variety of restaurants within walking distance, this may not be the answer, and you should look at the area's larger beach resorts or stays on the Hua Hin–Pranburi side instead · but for a trip that wants a quiet sea, still-intact nature, and the feeling of staying at a friend's place at an accessible price — Long Beach Inn meets that need almost perfectly, and it's why many call it "a secret you'd rather keep to yourself."

faqTitle: FAQ — Long Beach Inn Sam Roi Yot

faq.q: Where is Long Beach Inn and how do you get there?
faq.a: The inn is in Moo 4, Sam Roi Yot sub-district, Sam Roi Yot district, Prachuap Khiri Khan province, in the Phu Noi Beach area next to Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park · it's about 150 m from Phu Noi Beach (~5 min walk), about 40 km south down from Hua Hin (45–60 min drive), and about 30 minutes from Pranburi · from Bangkok it's around a 3–3.5 hr drive · having your own car is recommended, or arrange transfers with the inn in advance, since there are no shops or easy-to-flag public transport around it.

faq.q: Who is Long Beach Inn for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples and travellers who want a quiet seaside break in a small, owner-run stay, and nature lovers coming for Khao Sam Roi Yot and Phraya Nakhon Cave · it's pet-friendly, good for anyone wanting to bring a dog or cat · if you're after a big resort with full kids' activities, nightlife, or a variety of restaurants within walking distance, a larger beach resort or the Hua Hin side may suit you better.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,600/night for a Deluxe room at normal times (in some periods starting at roughly THB 1,400–2,000 depending on season) · there are Executive Rooms, a Suite with Jacuzzi and a Bridal Suite for couples · all rooms are non-smoking, with a private balcony, air conditioning, fridge, minibar, safe and free Wi-Fi · rooms fill up fast over long holidays since it's a small place, so book ahead and compare across platforms.

faq.q: What's Phu Noi Beach near Long Beach Inn like?
faq.a: Phu Noi Beach is a long, quiet sandy beach with nature still intact, with the Sam Roi Yot mountains as a backdrop · several foreign reviews say the beach is still quiet and almost empty, good for strolling, taking in the view and relaxing · it's about a 5 min walk from the inn · if you want to swim, check the tide times, and the inn also has a pool with jacuzzi in the garden to use.

faq.q: Is Long Beach Inn pet-friendly and is there breakfast?
faq.a: It's pet-friendly, so if you're bringing a dog or cat you should tell the inn at booking · breakfast is made-to-order (a la carte) — eggs, pancakes, bacon and a Western-style breakfast — which many reviews praise as tasty and more special than a buffet · you can eat in the garden or by the pool for the atmosphere.

faq.q: What's the service like at Long Beach Inn?
faq.a: It's the number-one selling point here, because the owner (reviews often name him Bram) runs the place and looks after guests personally · many reviews praise him as friendly and attentive, arranging rides to nearby sights and giving detailed advice on routes to Phraya Nakhon Cave · there's a resident dog, Bella, to welcome guests, giving it the easygoing feel of staying at a friend's place · the watch-out is that it's a small inn relying on a small team, so you may wait a bit at times, but overall the service is the reason it holds #2 in the area.
